newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli pig poster suspect fit to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Israeli pig poster suspect fit to stand trial.

text.p: The Israeli woman accused of pasting posters on Hebron storefronts depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig is mentally fit to stand trial, an Israeli court ruled on Wednesday.
Psychiatrists evaluated 26-year-old Tatyana Suskin during a week-long stay at a mental hospital this month.
"The decision was that she would stand trial after it was ruled there was no need to keep here in the mental hospital," said a court official.
The posters, pasted on June 27 across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of Hebron in the West Bank provoked an outpouring of Moslem rage and violent anti-Israeli protests.
Suskin is accused of committing a racist act, harming religious sensitivities, supporting a terrorist group and endangering life by stoning an Arab car.
The offences carry a maximum 26-year sentence.

"I regret nothing," she shouted to reporters at her first court appearance last month, wearing a a yellow shirt with the black clenched fist of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane.
Wednesday's ruling followed a decision by the army to charge an Israeli soldier who shot and wounded seven Arabs in Hebron earlier this year with attempted murder.

The army said on Tuesday a military court decided Noam Friedman, a 22-year-old conscript, was now fit to stand trial after ruling last February that he must be confined to a psychiatric hospital and would not be charged.
"Because of the clear public interest in this case and because in contrast to the past Friedman is now fit to stand trial, an indictment was issued," the army said in a statement.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian forces in January. Its troops remained in 20 percent of Hebron to guard 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in the heart of the town of more than 100,000 Palestinians.
Hebron is revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
